body:
extends Node3D
## Fathom Reef: a cozy, fully immersive underwater reef full of cute fish (no passthrough).
## Controls: left stick swim, right stick turn (snap) / up-down, trigger sprinkle fish food,
## grip blow bubbles, A/X call the fish, B show/hide help, Y bring Claude's build-log board.
##
## Desktop test (no headset): godot-gpu --xr-mode off --path . -- --shots=<dir> [--icon]

const Fish := preload("res://fish.gd")
const Reef := preload("res://reef.gd")
const Sfx := preload("res://sfx.gd")
const Link := preload("res://link.gd")
const HANDS := ["left_hand", "right_hand"]
const TIP := Vector3(0, 0, -0.05)


class Hand:
	var ok := false
	var aim := Transform3D()      # aim pose (finger along -Z)
	var grip_xf := Transform3D()  # grip pose
	var tip := Vector3.ZERO
	var vel := Vector3.ZERO
	var grip := 0.0
	var trigger := 0.0
	var stick := Vector2.ZERO
	var ax := false
	var by := false
	var menu := false
	var prev_tip := Vector3.ZERO
	var prev_ax := false
	var prev_by := false
	var prev_menu := false
	var food_t := 0.0
	var bubble_t := 0.0
	var bubbles: CPUParticles3D


var xr: XRInterface
var origin: XROrigin3D
var camera: XRCamera3D
var fish: Fish
var reef: Reef
var sfx: Sfx
var link: Link
var hands: Array[Hand] = [Hand.new(), Hand.new()]
var pointers: Array[Node3D] = []
var title: Node3D
var help_t := 18.0
var turn_ready := true
var placed := false
var age := 0.0
var shots_dir := ""
var make_icon := false
var desktop_spin := true


func _ready() -> void:
	for a in OS.get_cmdline_user_args():
		if a.begins_with("--shots="):
			shots_dir = a.substr(8)
		elif a == "--icon":
			make_icon = true
	_start_xr()
	reef = Reef.new()
	add_child(reef)
	fish = Fish.new()
	add_child(fish)
	sfx = Sfx.new()
	add_child(sfx)
	origin = XROrigin3D.new()
	add_child(origin)
	camera = XRCamera3D.new()
	camera.near = 0.03
	camera.far = 60.0
	camera.position = Vector3(0, 1.6, 0)
	origin.add_child(camera)
	var snow := reef.make_snow()
	camera.add_child(snow)
	for i in 2:
		pointers.append(_make_hand())
		var b := reef.make_bubbles(60, 5.0)
		b.emitting = false
		b.initial_velocity_min = 0.3
		b.initial_velocity_max = 0.7
		b.direction = Vector3(0, 0.3, -1)
		b.spread = 25.0
		pointers[i].add_child(b)
		b.position = TIP
		hands[i].bubbles = b
	_make_title()
	link = Link.new()
	link.main = self
	add_child(link)
	link.place_board(head_transform())
	fish.ate.connect(func(p: Vector3) -> void: sfx.play("nom", p, -4.0))
	fish.nibbled.connect(_on_nibble)
	if xr == null:
		if shots_dir != "":
			desktop_spin = false
			_run_test()


func _start_xr() -> void:
	xr = XRServer.find_interface("OpenXR")
	if xr != null and xr.is_initialized():
		get_viewport().use_xr = true
		DisplayServer.window_set_vsync_mode(DisplayServer.VSYNC_DISABLED)
		var oxr := xr as OpenXRInterface
		if oxr != null:
			oxr.session_begun.connect(func() -> void:
				var rates: Array = oxr.get_available_display_refresh_rates()
				if rates.has(90.0):
					oxr.display_refresh_rate = 90.0)
	else:
		xr = null
		print("OpenXR not available: running in desktop mode")


func head_transform() -> Transform3D:
	return origin.global_transform * camera.transform


func _make_hand() -> Node3D:
	## A pink dragon paw with a pointing finger and a little claw, in aim-pose space.
	var n := Node3D.new()
	var pink := StandardMaterial3D.new()
	pink.albedo_color = Color(1.0, 0.55, 0.75)
	pink.emission_enabled = true
	pink.emission = Color(0.25, 0.08, 0.15)
	var white := StandardMaterial3D.new()
	white.albedo_color = Color(1, 0.97, 0.92)
	var finger := MeshInstance3D.new()
	var cap := CapsuleMesh.new()
	cap.radius = 0.009
	cap.height = 0.085
	finger.mesh = cap
	finger.rotation.x = PI / 2
	finger.position = Vector3(0, 0, -0.012)
	finger.material_override = pink
	n.add_child(finger)
	var claw := MeshInstance3D.new()
	var cone := CylinderMesh.new()
	cone.top_radius = 0.0
	cone.bottom_radius = 0.006
	cone.height = 0.014
	claw.mesh = cone
	claw.rotation.x = -PI / 2
	claw.position = Vector3(0, 0.002, -0.054)
	claw.material_override = white
	n.add_child(claw)
	var palm := MeshInstance3D.new()
	var sph := SphereMesh.new()
	sph.radius = 0.045
	sph.height = 0.07
	palm.mesh = sph
	palm.scale = Vector3(0.9, 0.55, 1.1)
	palm.position = Vector3(0, -0.018, 0.06)
	palm.material_override = pink
	n.add_child(palm)
	n.visible = false
	add_child(n)
	return n


func _make_title() -> void:
	title = Node3D.new()
	add_child(title)
	var big := Label3D.new()
	big.text = "Fathom Reef"
	big.font_size = 160
	big.pixel_size = 0.0015
	big.outline_size = 24
	big.modulate = Color(1.0, 0.85, 0.95)
	big.outline_modulate = Color(0.1, 0.2, 0.35)
	title.add_child(big)
	var small := Label3D.new()
	small.text = "left stick: swim   right stick: turn / up-down\ntrigger: fish food   grip: bubbles   A/X: call the fish\nhold a finger still and the curious ones come for a nibble\nB: hide this help   Y: Claude's build log"
	small.font_size = 48
	small.pixel_size = 0.0015
	small.outline_size = 10
	small.modulate = Color(0.85, 0.97, 1.0)
	small.outline_modulate = Color(0.05, 0.12, 0.2)
	small.position = Vector3(0, -0.25, 0)
	title.add_child(small)
	for l: Label3D in [big, small]:
		l.shaded = false
	_place_title()


func _place_title() -> void:
	var h := head_transform()
	var f := -h.basis.z
	f.y = 0
	f = f.normalized() if f.length() > 0.01 else Vector3.FORWARD
	var p := h.origin + f * 2.2
	p.y = h.origin.y + 0.35
	title.global_position = p
	title.look_at(p + f, Vector3.UP)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- input

static func _f(v: Variant) -> float:
	if v == null:
		return 0.0
	if v is bool:
		return 1.0 if v else 0.0
	return float(v)


func _read_xr() -> void:
	for i in 2:
		var h := hands[i]
		h.ok = false
		var tr := XRServer.get_tracker(HANDS[i]) as XRPositionalTracker
		if tr == null:
			continue
		var have := false
		for pn in ["grip", "grip_pose", "default"]:
			var pose := tr.get_pose(pn)
			if pose != null and pose.has_tracking_data:
				h.grip_xf = origin.global_transform * pose.get_adjusted_transform()
				have = true
				break
		if not have:
			continue
		h.ok = true
		var ap := tr.get_pose("aim_pose")
		if ap == null:
			ap = tr.get_pose("aim")
		if ap != null and ap.has_tracking_data:
			h.aim = origin.global_transform * ap.get_adjusted_transform()
		else:
			h.aim = h.grip_xf * Transform3D(Basis(), Vector3(0, -0.03, -0.05))
		h.aim.basis = h.aim.basis.orthonormalized()
		h.tip = h.aim * TIP
		var ct := tr as XRControllerTracker
		if ct == null:
			continue
		h.grip = _f(ct.get_input("grip"))
		h.trigger = _f(ct.get_input("trigger"))
		var st: Variant = ct.get_input("primary")
		h.stick = st if st is Vector2 else Vector2.ZERO
		h.ax = _f(ct.get_input("ax_button")) > 0.5
		h.by = _f(ct.get_input("by_button")) > 0.5
		h.menu = _f(ct.get_input("menu_button")) > 0.5


func buzz(hand: int, amp := 0.4, secs := 0.05) -> void:
	if xr != null:
		xr.trigger_haptic_pulse("haptic", HANDS[hand], 0.0, amp, secs, 0.0)


func _on_nibble(hand: int, p: Vector3) -> void:
	sfx.play("boop", p, -2.0)
	buzz(hand, 0.35, 0.06)


func _process(dt: float) -> void:
	age += dt
	if xr != null:
		_read_xr()
		if not placed and age > 0.6 and camera.position.y > 0.25:
			placed = true
			_place_title()
			link.place_board(head_transform())
	elif desktop_spin and shots_dir == "":
		camera.rotation.y += dt * 0.08
	var L := hands[0]
	var R := hands[1]
	# swimming: left stick moves along the gaze (flattened), right stick snap-turns and rises/sinks
	var head := head_transform()
	var f := -head.basis.z
	f.y = 0
	f = f.normalized() if f.length() > 0.01 else Vector3.FORWARD
	var r := f.cross(Vector3.UP)
	var mv := (f * L.stick.y + r * L.stick.x) * 1.3
	if absf(R.stick.y) > 0.4:
		mv.y = R.stick.y * 0.9
	var o := origin.position + mv * dt
	var hr := Vector2(o.x, o.z)
	if hr.length() > 11.0:
		hr = hr.normalized() * 11.0
	origin.position = Vector3(hr.x, clampf(o.y, 0.0, 5.0), hr.y)
	if absf(R.stick.x) > 0.7 and turn_ready:
		turn_ready = false
		var pivot := head_transform().origin
		var ang := -deg_to_rad(30.0) * signf(R.stick.x)
		var t := Transform3D(Basis(Vector3.UP, ang), Vector3.ZERO)
		origin.global_transform = Transform3D(Basis(), pivot) * t * Transform3D(Basis(), -pivot) * origin.global_transform
	elif absf(R.stick.x) < 0.3:
		turn_ready = true
	# hands: food, bubbles, calling, menus
	var fish_hands: Array = []
	for i in 2:
		var h := hands[i]
		h.vel = (h.tip - h.prev_tip) / maxf(dt, 1e-3) if h.ok else Vector3.ZERO
		h.prev_tip = h.tip
		pointers[i].visible = h.ok
		if h.ok:
			pointers[i].global_transform = h.aim
		fish_hands.append({"ok": h.ok, "tip": h.tip, "vel": h.vel})
		h.food_t -= dt
		if h.ok and h.trigger > 0.6 and h.food_t <= 0.0:
			h.food_t = 0.18
			fish.drop_pellet(h.tip, -h.aim.basis.z * 0.25 + Vector3(randf_range(-0.05, 0.05), 0.05, randf_range(-0.05, 0.05)))
			sfx.play("plop", h.tip, -8.0)
		var blowing := h.ok and h.grip > 0.6
		h.bubbles.emitting = blowing
		h.bubble_t -= dt
		if blowing and h.bubble_t <= 0.0:
			h.bubble_t = randf_range(0.08, 0.2)
			sfx.play("bubble", h.tip, -10.0)
		if h.ax and not h.prev_ax:
			fish.call_fish(head.origin + f * 0.7 - Vector3(0, 0.2, 0))
			sfx.play("chime", h.tip, -4.0)
			buzz(i, 0.2, 0.1)
		if h.by and not h.prev_by:
			if i == 1:
				help_t = 0.0 if help_t > 0.0 else 30.0
				if help_t > 0.0:
					_place_title()
			else:
				link.place_board(head)
		h.prev_ax = h.ax
		h.prev_by = h.by
	help_t = maxf(help_t - dt, 0.0)
	title.visible = help_t > 0.0
	fish.step(dt, fish_hands, head.origin)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- scripted desktop test

var checks: Array[String] = []


func _check(what: String, ok: bool) -> void:
	checks.append("%s %s" % ["PASS" if ok else "FAIL", what])
	print(checks[-1])


func _frames(n: int) -> void:
	for i in n:
		await get_tree().process_frame


func _wait(secs: float) -> void:
	var t := age + secs
	while age < t:
		await get_tree().process_frame


func _fake_hand(h: Hand, tip: Vector3) -> void:
	h.ok = true
	h.aim = Transform3D(Basis(Vector3.RIGHT, -0.3), tip)
	h.aim.origin = tip - h.aim.basis * TIP
	h.tip = tip


func _shot(shot: String, cam_pos: Vector3, target: Vector3) -> Image:
	camera.global_position = cam_pos
	camera.look_at(target)
	await _frames(3)
	await RenderingServer.frame_post_draw
	var img := get_viewport().get_texture().get_image()
	DirAccess.make_dir_recursive_absolute(shots_dir)
	img.save_png(shots_dir.path_join(shot + ".png"))
	print("shot ", shot)
	return img


func _all_fish() -> Array[Vector3]:
	var out: Array[Vector3] = []
	for s in fish.species:
		for p in s.pos:
			out.append(p)
	return out


func _near(p: Vector3, r: float) -> int:
	var n := 0
	for q in _all_fish():
		if q.distance_to(p) < r:
			n += 1
	return n


func _run_test() -> void:
	await _frames(5)
	_check("fish spawned (%d)" % fish.fish_count(), fish.fish_count() >= 100)
	var before := _all_fish()
	await _wait(1.5)
	var after := _all_fish()
	var moved := 0.0
	for i in before.size():
		moved += before[i].distance_to(after[i])
	moved /= before.size()
	_check("fish swim (mean %.2f m in 1.5 s)" % moved, moved > 0.1)
	var inside := true
	for p in after:
		if p.y < 0.0 or p.y > 6.0 or Vector2(p.x, p.z).length() > 13.0:
			inside = false
	_check("fish stay inside the reef", inside)
	# frame rate of the whole scene on this GPU
	var f0 := Engine.get_frames_drawn()
	var t0 := Time.get_ticks_msec()
	await _wait(2.0)
	var fps := (Engine.get_frames_drawn() - f0) * 1000.0 / maxf(Time.get_ticks_msec() - t0, 1)
	print("desktop FPS %.1f" % fps)
	await _shot("overview", Vector3(0, 1.6, 0), Vector3(0, 1.2, -6))
	await _shot("back", Vector3(0, 1.6, 0), Vector3(2, 1.0, 6))
	await _shot("up", Vector3(0, 1.3, 0), Vector3(0.5, 6, -2.5))
	# curious fish come to a still finger
	var R := hands[1]
	var tip := Vector3(0.25, 1.3, -0.5)
	_fake_hand(R, tip)
	R.prev_tip = tip
	var near0 := _near(tip, 0.6)
	await _wait(8.0)
	var near1 := _near(tip, 0.6)
	_check("curious fish visit a still finger (%d -> %d within 0.6 m)" % [near0, near1], near1 > near0 and near1 >= 2)
	await _shot("finger", Vector3(0.05, 1.45, 0.05), tip)
	# a fast swipe scares them
	for k in 12:
		_fake_hand(R, tip + Vector3(sin(k * 0.8) * 0.4, 0, 0))
		await _frames(1)
	await _wait(0.6)
	var near2 := _near(tip, 0.6)
	_check("a fast swipe scatters them (%d -> %d)" % [near1, near2], near2 < near1)
	R.ok = false
	# feeding
	var eaten := [0]
	fish.ate.connect(func(_p: Vector3) -> void: eaten[0] += 1)
	var food_at := Vector3(-0.3, 1.4, -0.8)
	for k in 10:
		fish.drop_pellet(food_at + Vector3(randf_range(-0.1, 0.1), 0, randf_range(-0.1, 0.1)), Vector3.ZERO)
	await _wait(5.0)
	await _shot("feeding", Vector3(0.1, 1.55, 0.1), food_at - Vector3(0, 0.25, 0))
	await _wait(5.0)
	_check("fish eat the food (%d of 10 pellets)" % eaten[0], eaten[0] >= 5)
	# calling
	fish.call_fish(Vector3(0, 1.3, -0.8))
	await _wait(6.0)
	_check("A/X calls the fish (%d near)" % _near(Vector3(0, 1.3, -0.8), 1.0), _near(Vector3(0, 1.3, -0.8), 1.0) >= 8)
	# close-up of one of each species for a cuteness check
	for s in fish.species:
		var p: Vector3 = s.pos[0]
		var fw: Vector3 = s.fwd[0]
		var side := fw.cross(Vector3.UP).normalized()
		await _shot("cute_" + s.name, p + side * s.size * 3.2 - fw * s.size * 1.2 + Vector3(0, s.size * 0.4, 0), p)
	# link: log, eval and run a live script the same way Claude will from Termux
	var r: Dictionary = link._handle(JSON.stringify({"cmd": "log", "text": "hello from the test"}))
	_check("link log", r.ok and link.lines[-1].ends_with("hello from the test"))
	r = link._handle(JSON.stringify({"cmd": "eval", "expr": "fish.fish_count()"}))
	_check("link eval (%s)" % r.get("result", r.get("error")), r.ok and int(r.result) == fish.fish_count())
	var code := "extends Node3D\nvar main\nfunc _ready():\n\tvar m := MeshInstance3D.new()\n\tm.mesh = BoxMesh.new()\n\tadd_child(m)\n\tposition = Vector3(0, 1, -2)\n"
	r = link._run("test_cube", code, false)
	await _frames(2)
	var node := link.live_root.get_node_or_null("test_cube")
	_check("link run builds a live node", r.ok and node != null and node.get("main") == self)
	r = link._run("broken", "extends Node3D\nfunc _ready(:\n", false)
	_check("link rejects a broken script", not r.ok)
	if node:
		node.queue_free()
	link.add_line("all tests done")
	link.place_board(Transform3D(Basis(), Vector3(0, 1.6, 0)))
	await _shot("board", Vector3(-0.45, 1.6, 0.2), link.board.global_position)
	if make_icon:
		var s: Fish.Species = fish.species[0]
		var p: Vector3 = s.pos[0]
		var fw: Vector3 = s.fwd[0]
		var side := fw.cross(Vector3.UP).normalized()

What are the current goal parameters?  Is it going purely by distance?

No, it's mostly distance, with two small adjustments. Each robot's score is calculated like this:

**score = distance moved to the right − 0.3 × sideways drift + 0.5 × (fraction of the round spent upright)**

- **Distance:** how far the body's centre has moved along its lane toward the right edge of the stage, in metres. Going backwards scores negative.
- **Drift penalty:** for each metre the body wanders sideways out of its lane, 0.3 is subtracted.
- **Upright bonus:** up to +0.5 for staying up the whole round. It's small next to the distance term.
- **Falling ends the score:** once a robot falls, its score freezes at that moment and it stops being controlled.
  - A spider counts as fallen when its body drops below 12 cm or tilts more than about 75°.
  - A humanoid counts as fallen when its trunk drops below 55 cm or tilts that far.
- **Round length:** 12 seconds for spiders, 8 seconds for humanoids. The score is wherever the robot is at the end of the round, or at the moment it fell.
- **Selection:** after each round all robots are ranked by score. The best one is kept unchanged, and the all-time best is brought back with tiny tweaks. The rest of the next round are crossover-and-mutation copies of the top half.

**Weaknesses I can see:**
1. **The humanoids are rewarded for lunging.** The trunk only counts as fallen once its centre drops below 55 cm. A humanoid that dives forward gains roughly half a metre of distance on the way down, which beats the 0.5 upright bonus. At generation 75 that's probably a good part of what they've learned.
2. **Nothing rewards efficiency or style.** Flailing at full motor power costs nothing, so jittery or shaky gaits are as good as smooth ones.
3. **A single lucky run counts as much as a real gait.** Each network gets only one 8–12 second try, so a lucky stumble can win a round. The champion gets re-tested every round, which helps a little.

**Changes I'd suggest:**
- **For the humanoids:** score only distance gained while upright, with a fall penalty (say −1) and a larger reward for time spent up. That way, learning to balance comes first and walking second.
- **For both:** a small energy cost on motor effort, which pushes them toward smoother, more efficient gaits.
- **Optionally:** a gentle height reward to stop the spiders belly-sliding.

extends Node3D
## Fast-forward panel for the robot gyms: poke 1x / 2x / 4x / 8x with a fingertip.
## Uses main.set_sim_speed(k): physics ticks k times as often with the SAME 1/90 s step, so the
## robots' physics is exactly as stable as at 1x; only the CPU work grows. If the headset can't
## keep up (under 72 FPS for 1.5 s) it steps down a level by itself so VR stays comfortable.
## The readout shows the speed actually reached (simulated seconds per real second).

const SPEEDS := [1.0, 2.0, 4.0, 8.0]
const BTN := Vector2(0.075, 0.055)

var main
var level := 0
var buttons: Array[MeshInstance3D] = []
var mats: Array[StandardMaterial3D] = []
var readout: Label3D
var press_cool := 0.0
var slow_t := 0.0
var settle := 0.0
var ticks := 0
var win_t := 0.0
var actual := 1.0


func _ready() -> void:
	_build()
	_place()
	_apply(0)


func _place() -> void:
	var head: Transform3D = main.head_transform() if main else Transform3D(Basis(), Vector3(0, 1.6, 0))
	var f := -head.basis.z
	f.y = 0
	f = f.normalized() if f.length() > 0.01 else Vector3.FORWARD
	var right := f.cross(Vector3.UP)
	var p := head.origin + f * 0.5 + right * 0.4 + Vector3(0, -0.3, 0)
	# face the player, tilted back a little like a control desk
	global_transform = Transform3D(Basis.looking_at(f, Vector3.UP) * Basis(Vector3.RIGHT, -0.5), p)


func _build() -> void:
	var back := MeshInstance3D.new()
	var bm := BoxMesh.new()
	bm.size = Vector3(0.4, 0.2, 0.012)
	back.mesh = bm
	var bmat := StandardMaterial3D.new()
	bmat.albedo_color = Color(0.06, 0.1, 0.16)
	bmat.emission_enabled = true
	bmat.emission = Color(0.02, 0.05, 0.08)
	back.material_override = bmat
	back.position.z = -0.012
	add_child(back)
	var title := Label3D.new()
	title.text = "ROBOT FAST-FORWARD"
	title.font_size = 36
	title.pixel_size = 0.0008
	title.outline_size = 0
	title.modulate = Color(1.0, 0.7, 0.85)
	title.shaded = false
	title.position = Vector3(0, 0.075, 0)
	add_child(title)
	for i in SPEEDS.size():
		var b := MeshInstance3D.new()
		var m := BoxMesh.new()
		m.size = Vector3(BTN.x, BTN.y, 0.018)
		b.mesh = m
		var mat := StandardMaterial3D.new()
		mat.emission_enabled = true
		b.material_override = mat
		b.position = Vector3(-0.135 + i * 0.09, 0.01, 0)
		add_child(b)
		var l := Label3D.new()
		l.text = "%d×" % int(SPEEDS[i])
		l.font_size = 48
		l.pixel_size = 0.0008
		l.outline_size = 0
		l.modulate = Color.WHITE
		l.shaded = false
		l.position = Vector3(0, 0, 0.0095)
		b.add_child(l)
		buttons.append(b)
		mats.append(mat)
	readout = Label3D.new()
	readout.font_size = 28
	readout.pixel_size = 0.0008
	readout.outline_size = 0
	readout.modulate = Color(0.85, 0.95, 1.0)
	readout.shaded = false
	readout.position = Vector3(0, -0.06, 0)
	add_child(readout)


func _apply(i: int) -> void:
	level = i
	if main and main.has_method("set_sim_speed"):
		main.set_sim_speed(SPEEDS[i])
	elif SPEEDS[i] != 1.0 and main:
		main.link.add_line("fast-forward needs the updated app (main.set_sim_speed)")
		level = 0
	settle = 3.0
	slow_t = 0.0
	for k in mats.size():
		var on := k == level
		mats[k].albedo_color = Color(1.0, 0.45, 0.7) if on else Color(0.2, 0.32, 0.42)
		mats[k].emission = Color(0.6, 0.15, 0.35) if on else Color(0.03, 0.06, 0.09)
		buttons[k].position.z = -0.006 if on else 0.0


func _physics_process(_dt: float) -> void:
	ticks += 1


func _process(scaled_dt: float) -> void:
	var dt := scaled_dt / Engine.time_scale
	press_cool = maxf(press_cool - dt, 0.0)
	settle = maxf(settle - dt, 0.0)
	# measured speed: physics ticks per real second / base tick rate
	win_t += dt
	if win_t >= 1.0:
		actual = ticks / win_t / 90.0
		ticks = 0
		win_t = 0.0
	var fps := Engine.get_frames_per_second()
	if level > 0 and settle <= 0.0 and fps < 72:
		slow_t += dt
		if slow_t > 1.5:
			if main:
				main.link.add_line("fast-forward: headset struggling at %d×, stepping down" % int(SPEEDS[level]))
			_apply(level - 1)
	else:
		slow_t = 0.0
	readout.text = "chosen %d×   actual %.1f×   %d FPS" % [int(SPEEDS[level]), actual, fps]
	if main == null:
		return
	# poke a button with either index fingertip
	var inv := global_transform.affine_inverse()
	for h in main.hands:
		if not h.ok or press_cool > 0.0:
			continue
		var lt: Vector3 = inv * h.tip
		for i in buttons.size():
			var c := buttons[i].position
			if absf(lt.x - c.x) < BTN.x * 0.5 and absf(lt.y - c.y) < BTN.y * 0.5 and lt.z < 0.012 and lt.z > -0.04:
				press_cool = 0.4
				if i != level:

text:
Fast-forward is now in your headset. Your hunch was right: changing timescale on its own would have broken the physics.

**What I measured in Godot 4.7:**
- **Timescale on its own:** at 4× Godot keeps 90 physics steps per second but makes each step 4× longer (44 ms instead of 11 ms). The robots' stiff joint motors jitter, overshoot, and can blow up at that step size, and every result would differ from 1×.
- **Timescale plus tick rate:** if the physics tick rate goes up by the same factor (4× speed with 360 ticks/s), each step stays exactly 1/90 s. The robots get the same physics as at 1×, just run more often. All their timing (network every 3rd tick, round length, scoring) counts physics ticks, so their behaviour is identical at any speed.
- **The other catch:** timescale also speeds up everything else. I updated the app (v0.2, reinstalled) so the fish, bubbles, your swimming, the book and the build log all run on real time. Only the robots speed up. Training resumed from the saves after the reinstall.

**The panel:** "ROBOT FAST-FORWARD" sits in front of you, a little to the right, at hand height. Poke 1×, 2×, 3× or 4× with a fingertip. It shows the speed you chose, the speed actually reached, and the FPS. If the frame rate stays under 72 for 1.5 seconds, it steps down a level by itself, so VR stays comfortable.

**Measured on Fathom with both gyms running (22 robots):**

| Setting | Actual speed | Frame rate |
|---|---|---|
| 2× | 1.95× | 90 FPS, fully comfortable |
| 4× | 3.6× | 56 FPS, so it auto-steps down |
| 8× | — | about 37 FPS, so I swapped it for 3× |

The limit is the CPU, not physics stability. Each extra step costs the full physics and neural-network work for all 22 robots. If you want more speed later, the options are:
- run only one gym at a time
- run the networks less often
- let it train while you're in the headset doing something low-load

body:
cd ~/ClaudeProjects/fathom-reef && python3 - <<'EOF'
p='game/sfx.gd'; s=open(p).read()
old='''	var data := PackedByteArray()
	data.resize(n * 2)
	for i in n:
		var v := buf[i]
		if i < fade:
			var k := float(i) / fade
			v = buf[i] * k + buf[n + i] * (1.0 - k)
		data.encode_s16(i * 2, int(clampf(v, -1.0, 1.0) * 30000.0))'''
new='''	# PAD extra samples after loop_end repeat the loop start: the mixer interpolates a few
	# samples past loop_end when it wraps, and without this it read off the end of the buffer
	# (SIGSEGV in the AudioTrack thread on a motorola razr, right at the 8 s wrap).
	var pad := 256
	var data := PackedByteArray()
	data.resize((n + pad) * 2)
	for i in n + pad:
		var j := i % n
		var v := buf[j]
		if j < fade:
			var k := float(j) / fade
			v = buf[j] * k + buf[n + j] * (1.0 - k)
		data.encode_s16(i * 2, int(clampf(v, -1.0, 1.0) * 30000.0))'''
assert old in s; s=s.replace(old,new)
# one-shots get a short silent tail for the same reason (they play with pitch_scale up to 1.2)
s=s.replace('''	var n := int(length * RATE)
	var data := PackedByteArray()
	data.resize(n * 2)
	var rng := RandomNumberGenerator.new()
	rng.seed = hash(length)''','''	var n := int(length * RATE)
	var data := PackedByteArray()
	data.resize((n + 256) * 2)   # zeroed tail: room for the mixer's interpolation look-ahead
	var rng := RandomNumberGenerator.new()
	rng.seed = hash(length)''')
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF

text:
Reef Gym runs on your phone now. It had been crashing about 9 seconds after launch, and that's fixed. I tested it by tapping through adb and taking screenshots.

**The crash:** the background ambient sound is an 8-second loop. Each time it wrapped back to the start, Godot's audio mixer read a few samples past the end of the sound data. On your razr that happened to run into memory it wasn't allowed to read, which crashed the app. I padded every sound with extra samples past the end, so those reads stay inside the data. After the fix it ran 40+ seconds through five loop wraps with no crash.

**On your razr:**
- **Normal speed:** a steady 60 FPS, with both gyms training.
- **4×:** reached a true 4.0× at 30 FPS, then stepped itself down to 3× because of the frame-rate safeguard. 3× is about the phone's comfortable limit.
- **New rules camera:** zooms onto the right-hand stage as intended.
- **Book:** opens as two-page spreads, and swiping turns the pages. The text is large and readable on your screen.
- **Fish colours look right on the phone:** pastel puffers and yellow fish. The dark, neon-green fish I kept seeing were a quirk of the Termux desktop's graphics driver, not a bug in the app. I'd still check them in the headset sometime.

**The headset app** had the same latent audio bug, so I rebuilt it with the fix (v0.3). I installed it while the reef app wasn't running, and your robot training saves are kept.

Training on the phone started from scratch: its log shows both gyms around generation 7–10 so far. Whenever the headset app is open, I can copy Fathom's trained networks into the phone version so it picks up from there.

The phone pairing and the crash details are in my notes, everything is committed, and I sent you a popup in the headset.
